kurz: Fruit ripens, browns and sets by the same rules: ripening gas, enzymes, acid and pectin.
bild_im_kopf: Like a fuse: once lit, it keeps burning even after picking.
was_passiert: Many fruits keep ripening after harvest. A gas called [[ethylen|ethylene]] sets this off: starch turns into sugar and the flesh softens. Once cut, many fruits brown through an enzyme. Their pectin can be set into jam with sugar and acid.
warum_wichtig: Knowing the rules means storing fruit longer, ripening it on purpose and keeping it bright.
faustregeln: Store apples apart from other fruit, unless you want it to ripen.
